mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST) below 1.5 million units signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depress consumer spending and corporate margins, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of sustained unemployment above 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered manufacturing contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL above 3% and FEDFUNDS above 3% for three consecutive months signals a high-inflation, high-rate regime that erodes real corporate earnings and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% AND FEDFUNDS > 3% for three consecutive months
regime_hint: high inflation and high interest rate regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of co-elevated CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS above 3%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 5% while personal income (PAYEMS) grows below 2% monthly signals a shift from spending to saving, implying weaker consumption and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-mo MA +5% AND PAYEMS monthly change < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered episodes of increased savings and subdued income growth.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% for three consecutive months during a period of stable inflation (CPIAUCSL change within ±0.2%) signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for three consecutive months AND |CPIAUCSL monthly change| ≤ 0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered episodes of robust employment growth with stable inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 5% for four consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which feeds into broader demand expansion and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change > 5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of sustained above-5% monthly housing starts growth.
